transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m barely sleeping in any way that actually helps. I mean, I’m in bed, technically, but I’ll lie there for hours with my mind running through client models and numbers and assumptions, like I’m still at my desk, and I can’t seem to shut it off.

And then even when I do fall asleep, I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach all tight, like I’m already bracing for the day. By the time I get to work, I feel like I never really rested at all. It’s just been wearing me down, and I didn’t know what else to do.
Do you feel anxious or worried during the day, outside of when you're lying awake at night?

I don’t really know how to separate it, honestly. During the day I’m busy enough that I don’t always think, “Oh, I’m anxious,” but I’m definitely tense a lot. It’s like I’m constantly trying to keep everything from slipping, especially at work. I’ll be looking at one set of figures and already worrying about the next thing, or whether I missed something, or whether someone’s going to ask a question I should’ve anticipated.

So… yes, I guess there is worry during the day, but it feels almost normal to me at this point, if that makes sense. Like it’s just the background noise of my day. I don’t always notice it until I realize my shoulders are up around my ears or I’ve been rereading the same line over and over because my mind is already ten steps ahead.
Do you find yourself avoiding certain tasks or situations because they make you feel anxious or overwhelmed?

Yes. I mean… I don’t think of it as “avoiding” at first, because I tell myself I’m just prioritizing or I’ll get to it when I have a clearer head, but honestly, yes.

At work, the bigger models and presentations have become this thing I almost circle around. I’ll open the file, look at it, feel completely overwhelmed by how much could be wrong or how many assumptions someone might challenge, and then I’ll go answer emails or tweak some smaller thing that doesn’t matter as much. And then of course the important work slips, which makes everything worse. I actually got a formal performance warning recently because my models and presentations have been late or not where they need to be. That was… humiliating, honestly. I’ve always been someone people could rely on for that.

And outside work, I’ve basically stopped showing up for things that used to keep me steady. I used to volunteer teaching, and I had yoga, and a book club. They weren’t huge things, but they made my life feel like it had something in it besides spreadsheets and deadlines. Now I avoid them because the thought of having to be “on,” or answer people asking where I’ve been, or just manage another commitment feels like too much. So I don’t go, and then I feel worse because my life has gotten very small.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like headaches or stomach problems during the day, not just when waking up in the morning?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I don’t think I’ve been tracking it that clearly. The morning stomach-tightness stands out because it’s so immediate when I wake up, so I notice that. During the day, I’m often just pushing through whatever is happening, so I don’t always stop and think, “This is a physical symptom.”

I wouldn’t want to say yes in a definite way if I’m not sure. I guess I notice tension in my body sometimes, but as far as actual headaches or stomach problems during the day… I don’t know. Nothing specific is jumping out at me right now.
Have you been avoiding social interactions or gatherings because you feel anxious about them?

Yes… I have. I mean, I don’t always label it as anxiety in the moment, but that’s probably what it is. I’ve stopped going to things I used to actually care about — volunteer teaching, yoga, book club. Those were sort of the pieces of my life that made me feel like I wasn’t just work and exhaustion, you know? And now even the thought of showing up feels like too much.

Part of it is worrying that people will ask where I’ve been, or that I’ll have to explain myself, or just make conversation and seem normal. So I tell myself I’m too busy or I’ll go next week, but then I don’t. And it’s not helping — my life has gotten really narrow.

Work has been affected too. I’ve had a formal performance warning because my models and presentations keep slipping, and I think some of that is the same pattern — avoiding things that feel too overwhelming, then falling further behind. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, because I used to be much more reliable than this.
Have you ever had a sudden feeling of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I’ve had something that clearly fits that, like a sudden wave of terror that peaks really fast and feels like an “attack,” if that’s what you mean.

I do get overwhelmed, and sometimes it can feel like everything is too much, but it’s more… it builds, or it’s tied to a situation I’m already dreading. I’m not thinking of a specific time where out of nowhere I had intense fear or discomfort that shot up within minutes. At least nothing that stands out to me that way.
Do you ever feel like you're observing yourself from outside your body or like you're in a dream?

I don’t think so. Or at least… not in a clear way that I would describe like that. I know what you mean, I think — like feeling detached from yourself, or unreal, or like you’re watching yourself from somewhere else — and that’s not really something I’ve noticed.

There are times when I feel kind of numb or like I’m going through the motions, but I wouldn’t say I feel outside my body or like I’m in a dream. It’s more just… I’m there, I’m aware of what’s happening, I just may not feel very connected or engaged. But no, I can’t think of a time where I literally felt like I was observing myself from outside or that things around me weren’t real.
Do you ever feel like you're disconnected from your thoughts or feelings?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I mean, I definitely feel dulled sometimes, like my reactions are slower or flatter than they should be, but I don’t know if that’s the same as being disconnected from my thoughts or feelings.

My thoughts are usually very much there — almost too much there — but feelings can be harder to access or name, if that makes sense. Like I’ll know intellectually that something should make me happy or upset, and I can talk through it logically, but emotionally it feels muted or far away. But I still feel like they’re mine. I don’t feel separate from them in the way you might mean.

So… I don’t think I’ve noticed a true disconnection, exactly. More like I’m tired and kind of numbed out at times, but not detached from myself.
Have you experienced any physical symptoms like fatigue during the day?

Yes. Very much. I mean, that’s honestly one of the main reasons I came in — I barely sleep in any way that actually helps anymore.

I’ll go to bed exhausted, but then I just lie there awake, replaying work in my head… client models, numbers, things I need to fix, conversations I had or need to have. It’s like my brain won’t shut down. And then even if I do fall asleep, I’ll wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach tight, already feeling like I’m behind before the day has even started.

So by the time I get to work, I feel like I never really rested. I’m physically there, but I feel worn out during the day, like I’m dragging myself through it.
Have you ever had a sudden, intense feeling of fear or discomfort that seemed to come out of nowhere?

I don’t think so… not in the way you’re describing, like a sudden wave of terror out of nowhere.

I do get tense or uneasy sometimes, especially when I’m already worn down, but it usually feels tied to something I’m thinking about or dealing with. It’s not like I’m sitting there and then suddenly I’m overwhelmed by fear for no reason. I wouldn’t describe it as intense fear, exactly.

Maybe discomfort, yes, but more gradual, more like it builds or sits there in the background. I don’t think I’ve had those sudden episodes where it comes on sharply and unexpectedly.
Have you ever had a panic attack?

I don’t think I have, no. At least not what I understand a panic attack to be.

I’ve had periods where I feel really uncomfortable or keyed up, but it’s not like this sudden, overwhelming rush where I feel like I’m losing control or something terrible is happening. It’s more… I don’t know, a steady tension, or being worn down and uneasy. If panic attack means something very specific, maybe I’m not describing it correctly, but I wouldn’t say I’ve had one.
Do you think your physical symptoms, like the tension and fatigue, are related to your worries about work or are they something you experience separately?

I think they’re very much connected to work, yes. Not separate, or at least it doesn’t feel separate to me.

The fatigue is mostly because I’m not sleeping in any useful way anymore. I’ll get into bed already exhausted, and then instead of actually resting, I’m lying there going over client models, numbers, what I may have missed, what I need to fix the next morning. It just keeps looping. And then if I do fall asleep, I often wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach tight, like my body has already started the workday before I’ve even opened my laptop.

So by the time I’m actually at work, I feel like I never really slept. It’s not just being tired like I had a busy week — it’s more like I never got to recover in the first place.
Are you avoiding social interactions because you fear being judged or evaluated by others?

I’m not sure I’d put it that way. I don’t think I’m avoiding people specifically because I’m afraid they’ll judge me, at least not in a clear, conscious way.

I mean, I can be self-conscious sometimes, like anyone, especially in professional settings where I feel like I’m supposed to have everything together. But if I pull back socially, it doesn’t usually feel like, “Oh, they’re going to evaluate me,” or “They’ll think badly of me.” It’s more that I just don’t always have the energy for it, or I don’t feel up to carrying a conversation.

So… I wouldn’t say fear of being judged is the main reason. If anything, I sometimes worry I won’t be very good company, but that feels a little different than being afraid of scrutiny.
Do you think you avoid social situations because you're afraid of what others might think of you?

I guess… not really, no. Or at least I don’t experience it as, “I can’t go because people will think something bad about me.”

If I avoid things, it’s usually more vague than that. Like I’ll look at a dinner or a work gathering or even just meeting someone for coffee and think, “I don’t have it in me.” I might worry a little that I’ll seem flat or distracted or not very engaging, but it’s not this strong fear that they’re judging me. It’s more that the whole thing feels effortful, and I don’t trust myself to be present.

So I wouldn’t say fear of what others think is the main driver. There might be a little self-consciousness around the edges, but not enough that I’d call it the reason I avoid people.
Do you feel anxious most of the time, even when there's no apparent reason to be anxious?

I’m not sure I’d say “most of the time,” no. I mean, I do get anxious, but it usually feels like there’s something attached to it — some reason I can point to, even if maybe the reaction is bigger than it needs to be.

When you say “no apparent reason,” that’s where I hesitate, because I don’t usually feel anxious just out of nowhere, like sitting quietly and suddenly panicking for no reason. It’s more that my mind finds something to hook onto, or there’s already something in the background that feels unresolved. So I wouldn’t describe myself as anxious all the time without a cause.

I guess I’m often tense or on edge, but in my head there’s usually a “because.” Whether that because is reasonable is another question.
Do you feel anxious in situations where you are not being evaluated or judged, such as when you are alone or doing something you enjoy?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that, because I don’t think I track it that clearly in the moment.

If I’m alone, I can feel uneasy sometimes, but I don’t always know whether I’d call it anxiety exactly. It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking someone is judging me, obviously, because no one’s there. And if I’m doing something I normally enjoy, I can still feel kind of unsettled or distracted, but again, I don’t know if that’s anxiety or just… not being able to fully relax.

So I guess yes, I can feel tense or uncomfortable even when there’s no evaluation happening, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a clear pattern where I’m anxious in all those situations. It’s more blurry than that for me.
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about work or any specific problems?

I’m not sure I can separate it that cleanly, honestly. If I’m not actively thinking about work or some specific problem, I can still have this sort of background uneasiness, but I don’t always know what it’s attached to. It’s not like I can always say, “I’m anxious right now because of X,” but it also doesn’t feel completely random either.

Sometimes I’ll think I’m not thinking about anything in particular, and then if I really pay attention, there’s some vague pressure in the background — like something I’ve forgotten, or something I should be doing, or just a sense that I’m not settled. But I don’t know whether that counts as anxiety, or just tension, or just not being able to fully relax.

So… I guess the most honest answer is I don’t know. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where I’m anxious even when my mind is totally clear. My mind is almost never totally clear, if that makes sense.
Do you feel anxious when you are in situations that have nothing to do with work?

I’m not sure. I mean, yes, I can feel anxious outside of work situations, but I don’t know if it’s because the situation has nothing to do with work, or because my mind still brings work into it somehow, if that makes sense.

Like if I’m at the grocery store or at home trying to watch something, I might feel tense, but I don’t always stop and identify, “Oh, this is separate from work.” Sometimes it’s just this general discomfort or restlessness, and then if I look closer, maybe there’s some work thought in the background, or maybe there isn’t. It’s hard to tell.

So I wouldn’t say work is the only thing that makes me anxious, but I also can’t give a clean yes, like, “I’m anxious in completely unrelated situations for no reason.” It’s usually muddled together in my head.
Do you feel anxious when you are in completely relaxed or leisure situations with no deadlines or expectations?

I’m not sure I really have situations that feel completely relaxed in that clean way, if that makes sense. Like, I can be doing something that’s supposed to be leisure — watching a show, sitting outside, having a quiet evening — and there might not be an actual deadline or anyone expecting something from me right then. But I don’t always experience it as fully relaxed.

Whether I’d call that anxiety, I don’t know. Sometimes it’s more like I’m waiting for something, or I can’t quite settle into it. But I don’t know if that’s because there’s some expectation in the back of my mind, or because I’m just not very good at switching off.

So I guess I can’t give you a clear yes or no. I haven’t really noticed, “Oh, I’m anxious even when everything is totally relaxed.” It’s more that those situations don’t always feel as relaxed to me as they probably should.
Do you feel anxious when you are engaged in activities that you typically enjoy and that have no connection to work or other stressors in your life?

I’m not sure I can answer that very cleanly. I mean, I do have things that I typically enjoy, or at least used to think of as enjoyable, and they don’t have an obvious connection to work or anything stressful. But when I’m doing them, I don’t always know whether what I’m feeling is anxiety exactly.

Sometimes I’ll be doing something that should just be pleasant — something quiet, or distracting, or something I picked because I wanted to enjoy it — and I still don’t feel fully settled. But I don’t know if that means I’m anxious during enjoyable activities, or if I’m just not really able to relax into them. It’s like part of me is still monitoring something in the background, but I can’t always name what that thing is.

So… I guess I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where I can say, “Yes, even when I’m doing something I enjoy and there’s no stressor attached, I feel anxious.” It’s more blurry than that. I can feel uneasy or not entirely comfortable, but I don’t always know what to attribute it to.

But I don’t know whether that counts as anxiety, or just tension, or just not being able to fully relax.

So… I guess the most honest answer is I don’t know. I haven’t noticed a clear pattern where I’m anxious even when my mind is totally clear. My mind is almost never totally clear, if that makes sense.
